title: Catalyst spark notes: mini requests and priority heuristics
content:
Summary:
Quick, messy rollup of lightweight customer asks from the last three weeks of field calls (EMEA + NA). Focus is on low-effort patches that unblock customers or reduce false positives in our runtime heuristics. This is NOT final — meant to seed 1–2 micro-experiments for next sprint.

Top micro-requests (ranked by frequency x severity):
1) "kv prefetch toggle" — Customers building chat apps want an explicit toggle to pre-warm KV/prefix caches per conversation on session creation. Reported benefit: reduced tail latency for the first 10 user messages. (3 customers asked directly; 6 mentioned in Slack).
2) "per-route soft SLOs" — Platform teams want a way to mark routes as "best-effort" vs "guaranteed" so we can use cheaper model variants when under load. Use-case: internal analytics bot vs payment auth.
3) "streaming reconnect hints" — Long-running streaming chat sessions drop when network hiccups happen; customers want client-side hints (retry-after + last-token-id) so they can resume without confusing duplicate outputs.
4) "cost-preview in Console" — Non-technical PMs requested a cost preview when toggling quantization/kv settings for a route. Show estimated % change in tokens-per-dollar.
5) "ramp option for canary larger than 1%" — Ops wants a canary knob by QPS rather than % of requests so heavy traffic teams can stage large-volume canaries safely.

Representative customer quotes (paraphrased):
- "If the first few replies are slow, our users think the bot is broken — warming caches would help." — fintech beta customer
- "We want to test cheaper models on non-critical flows but maintain strict SLOs on auth routes." — enterprise platform team
- "Reconnects are killing UX on flaky mobile networks." — marketplace app

Problem hypotheses / why these matter:
- KV prefetch: many apps have a predictable prefix (system message + user metadata). Preloading KV reduces first-token generation cost and decreases retransmits from client backoff logic. If true, we can reduce 95th percentile by 20–40ms on warm-up requests.
- Per-route soft SLOs: enables automated fallbacks to cheaper variants; expected to reduce overall bill by 5–12% for customers with mixed-criticality flows.
- Streaming reconnect hints: reduces user-visible duplication and retry storms; expected to drop support tickets related to streaming by ~30% for affected customers.

Quick patches / experiment ideas (<= 2-week spikes):
A) KV prefetch prototype: add a boolean on route config "prefetch_kv_on_session_start" that runs a lightweight precompute (non-blocking) to warm KV for top-n recent system+user tokens. Scope: beta only, opt-in. Instrumentation: time-to-first-token, redis K/V hit rates, customer-perceived latency (via Cs logs). Owner: Jonas.
B) Route dev console cost preview: mock-up a simple slider in Console that shows "estimated per-1000-requests cost delta" when toggling quantization and batching. Data source: current billing per-model per-token + sample traffic distribution. Owner: Marta.
C) Streaming reconnect RFC + client hint header: add header X-RI-STREAM-RESUME with last-seen-token-id and suggested retry-window. Backend emits a short resume token that clients can post to resume. Minimal server change: emit token id in stream metadata; client library change to attempt resume. Owner: Priya (coordinate with SDKs).

Metrics to track (primary/secondary):
- Primary: 95th latency on first chat message (ms), per-route cost delta (%), number of streaming-reconnect tickets per week
- Secondary: KV hit ratio, canary QPS distribution, developer time to flip canary

Risk notes and open questions (notes-to-self style):
- Prefetching increases memory pressure; need to quantify KV cache eviction impact on hot models.
- Resume tokens could expose subtle replay attacks if not bound to session/identity — consult security (quick ping to security required).
- Cost preview must avoid misleading estimates — include confidence band; show assumptions.

Implementation constraints / quick wins:
- Do minimal server work first: emit resume token metadata during streaming response and add opt-in flag for prefetch. Avoid complicated orchestration for initial spike.
- Use existing billing telemetry to compute delta; don't build new pipelines for the spike.

Action items (who / when / notes):
- Jonas: spike KV prefetch prototype (2 days) + initial perf numbers (due 2029-03-28).
- Marta: Console mock (Figma) + sample cost calc (1 day) (due 2029-03-26).
- Priya: draft streaming-reconnect RFC and coordinate with SDK owners (due 2029-04-02).
- Aisha: security sync request + link to Confluence ticket (in flight).

Related threads / refs (quick links):
- Slack: #cs-field-notes thread-4032 (contains raw customer call notes)
- Jira: JIRA-CS-1129 (customer X: streaming disconnects)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probe-scripts/pull/78 (tooling to sample first-token times)

Open items for next discussion (triage list):
- Decide opt-in cadence: per-route vs per-project prefetch
- Define resume token lifecycle and binding to session identity
- Acceptable memory overhead for prefetch (target < 5% of route memory footprint)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Might be able to pair cost-preview with "simulate 7-day traffic" feature in Console to provide concrete delta (low effort if we sample).
- If KV prefetch reduces first-token latency reliably, we should surface an A/B study to quantify UX impact on retention.

End of notes — this doc is intentionally terse. Use as seed for sprint planning and link to CS playbook when we have prototypes.
